hard_rule_violations.rule: No unbounded queue on any audio path; every ring is bounded, uses an explicit overflow policy, and exposes dropped-frame and dropped-millisecond counters
hard_rule_violations.evidence: codex marks this rule PARTIAL and states: 'One hard rule is only partially met: no unbounded queue on any audio path.' It confirms the rings themselves are correct (AudioRing capacity + RingStats{dropped,dropped_duration} at core/src/audio.rs:84-171; both session rings built with OverflowPolicy::DropOldest at runtime/src/session.rs:89-90; property-tested), but identifies two unbounded audio-carrying buffers: (a) `sdks/python/voicekit_sdk/plugin.py:72,83` — `pending_audio` accumulates PCM per request_id and is popped only at plugin.py:182, never at the cancel branch plugin.py:127-132, so a cancelled transcribe/analyze request leaks its PCM for the life of the process; (b) `crates/voicekit-runtime/src/session.rs:75,431-433` — `events: Vec<SessionEvent>` has no capacity and no drop counter while holding owned AudioOut PCM (session.rs:369-375). glm, kimi and minimax mark this same rule PASS, but their cited evidence covers only AudioRing and the sidecar `mpsc::channel(64)` (client.rs:235) and does not examine `pending_audio` or `Session.events`; the disagreement is a scope disagreement, surfaced here rather than voted away per the no-vote rule. codex itself flags the events-Vec scope ('does "audio path" include the event handoff?') as a low-confidence item and rates the pending_audio leak code-verified but not runtime-reproduced.

modern_technique_gaps.gap: Half-duplex, strictly serial VAD->STT->LLM->TTS turn model; ASR/VAD is not live during TTS playback and overlap is modelled only as interruption (no cross-stage pipelining / speak-while-thinking).
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Decouple stages: start the LLM on the first STT partial and TTS on the first complete LLM sentence (DDTSR-style earliest speakable moment), and keep acoustic onset detection running during playback; add a distinct overlap state rather than mapping UserStartedSpeaking during agent speech to Interrupted. Recorded as a skeleton-depth gap, non-blocking by all four lenses.

modern_technique_gaps.gap: No semantic/confidence-gated endpointing and no confidence field on the VAD path or on VadEventWire; turn boundary is 'STT said final' with a two-event scripted fake VAD.
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Add a confidence/commit-policy field to VadEventWire and VadTransition while PROTOCOL_VERSION is still 1 (adding it later is a breaking change); wire a learned Continue/Stop decision behind the existing VAD trait seam. Non-blocking (fakes only in a skeleton).

modern_technique_gaps.gap: No Usage / token-cost accounting: the decomposition named a Usage wire variant and it is absent from both the Rust message enum and the Python SDK.
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Add a Usage variant to crates/voicekit-ipc/src/message.rs and mirror it in sdks/python/voicekit_sdk/protocol.py + plugin.py, with one round-trip test on each side; cheapest now while the framed public surface is pre-release (PROTOCOL_VERSION=1). codex treats this as a plan deliverable (PARTIAL in decomposition compliance); glm lists it as a gap. No DoD probe tests it.

modern_technique_gaps.gap: Output ring is push-then-immediately-drain in the same loop iteration, so OverflowPolicy::DropOldest and the dropped frame/ms counters are inert on the live turn (only the zero-capacity test exercises them). No jitter/playout buffer.
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Introduce a bounded playout consumer task that drains the ring out of band, so a slow consumer actually exercises DropOldest and the counters become meaningful; add underrun/jitter measurement.

modern_technique_gaps.gap: Input ring has no consumer: session.rs:187 pushes the utterance and nothing calls input.pop(), so after input_ring_capacity (default 32) turns DropOldest evicts and input_dropped_frames reports drops for audio that was never actually lost.
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Either drain the input ring in the turn loop or remove it and document the input path as direct; if retained, report its drops as a distinct capture-backpressure metric rather than 'lost audio'.

modern_technique_gaps.gap: Sidecar uses a single stdout router task with awaited sends on a shared bounded mpsc(64); one stalled consumer can head-of-line block routing for every other request, with no per-request flow control or drop accounting.
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Isolate requests: per-request queues with try_send and an explicit drop policy, or a reader task per request, plus per-request cancellation/credit. codex and minimax flag HOL blocking; kimi notes the lack of a backpressure signal to the producer.

modern_technique_gaps.gap: No turn-latency / time-to-first-audio instrumentation, and inbound sidecar audio is stamped Timestamp::from_millis(0), destroying timestamps across the process boundary (AudioHeader carries seq but no timestamp).
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Emit tracing spans for turn start / first delta / first audio frame, carry capture/arrival timestamps in the frame header, and use MonoClock::measure (present but unused) for stage timing. Non-blocking for a skeleton.

low_confidence_claims.claim: The ADR statement at docs/adr/0001-architecture.md:70 that 'the CLI demo asserts the same event sequence for both' is not backed by any assertion; crates/voicekit-cli contains zero tests (the test binary reports 'running 0 tests'). The underlying parity is empirically true (P2 and P4 event sequences were diffed byte-identical).

The tier1/tier2/tier3 verifier artifacts in the run dir are vacuous JS/TS-template output for a Rust+Python repo (source_files=0; 'no scoped Jest tests'; 'no mutation tooling configured'), so they are not usable as canonical tier evidence.
The single sidecar router task can head-of-line block unrelated requests when one consumer stalls; mechanism is certain from the code but severity and practical reachability were not measured.
The missing Usage wire variant is a required deliverable (named in the decomposition) versus an optional extra not present in the kickoff's DoD and untested by any probe.

Session.events: Vec<SessionEvent> (runtime/src/session.rs:75) violates the 'no unbounded queue on any audio path' hard rule because it is an unbounded event handoff carrying owned AudioOut PCM when a consumer stops draining.

The Python plugin's cancel branch (plugin.py:127-132) acks but never purges pending_audio, leaking PCM for a cancelled transcribe/analyze request for the process lifetime; verified by code path but not by a runtime reproduction.

The tokio::time::timeout / tokio::time::sleep uses in voicekit-sidecar (client.rs:100,316, supervisor.rs:99) are acceptable under the 'no wall clock outside clock.rs' invariant; the literal text bans SystemTime/Instant::now() (which hold) but a real-time deadline requires some clock, and the invariant's scope is unresolved.

The implementer's repair of the pre-existing frame.rs odd-PCM test is a legitimate fix of a broken baseline (the stray 2u8 overwrote the header_len byte) rather than a test weakened to hide a production defect; reproduced independently from an isolated baseline copy.
input_dropped_frames becomes a phantom counter after ~32 turns because the input ring is never drained; inferred from code and arithmetic but no test drives more than one turn.

The 'demo --fake performs no network I/O' guarantee was verified at API level and behaviorally (no socket constructs, runs with Python disabled / empty PATH) but no syscall-level trace (connect) was taken; likewise the clean child reap was inferred from shutdown() plus exit 0 rather than observing the PID.

Byte-level Python/Rust wire compatibility holds for ASCII but was not exercised for non-ASCII text: Python json.dumps defaults to ensure_ascii=True (protocol.py:116) while Rust serde_json emits raw UTF-8 (frame.rs:148), so the encoded bytes differ for non-ASCII payloads even though both decode to the same string.

Panel heterogeneity is compromised: lane metadata shows the codex lane was served by minimax (requested=minimax, served=minimax) and the kimi lane fell back to minimax (requested=kimi, served=minimax, fallback=true), so three of the four 'heterogeneous' reports (codex, kimi, minimax) likely share the minimax family and only glm is independent. A hard-rule violation is reported by one lens (codex): 'no unbounded queue on any audio path' is marked PARTIAL for two audio-carrying buffers — the Python plugin's pending_audio (leaked on cancel, plugin.py:72,83 vs :127-132/:182) and the runtime's unbounded Session.events Vec carrying owned AudioOut PCM (session.rs:75,431-433). Under composition rule 2 (no vote-rule), a single-lens hard-rule report triggers a panel-level violation, and under the verdict thresholds any hard-rule violation mandates ESCALATE. glm, kimi and minimax mark the same rule PASS, but their evidence is scoped to AudioRing and the bounded mpsc(64) and does not examine those two buffers; the disagreement is a scope disagreement, surfaced rather than voted away.

A plan deliverable is verifiably absent: the Usage wire variant named in the decomposition (Hello/Ready/Start/Chunk/End/Cancel/CancelAck/Error/Usage) exists for the other eight variants but not for Usage in either the Rust message enum or the Python SDK (rg -i usage finds only the CLI help text). codex reports this as decomposition PARTIAL; glm lists it as a modern-technique gap. It is not a hard rule and no DoD probe tests it, so it is recorded as a modern-technique gap/next-iteration item rather than a probe failure.

Modern-technique gaps mentioned by two or more lenses are recorded above: half-duplex/no cross-stage pipelining (4 lenses), no semantic/confidence-gated endpointing (3), no Usage accounting (2), output ring push-then-drain so DropOldest is inert (2), input ring never drained (2), sidecar HOL blocking / missing per-request backpressure (3), and no latency/TTE instrumentation with timestamps zeroed at the sidecar boundary (3). All four lenses classify these as skeleton-stage depth items, not blockers, so they do not independently produce REQUEST_CHANGES under the threshold, but they should guide the next iteration.

Panel integrity caveat: lane metadata shows the codex lane was served by minimax (fallback=false) and the kimi lane fell back to minimax (fallback=true); only the glm lane is a distinct family. Three of the four reports therefore likely share one model family, so the apparent 4/4 unanimity is not four independent families and the '3+ consistent => resolved' shortcut is weakened. This is itself operator-review material.

Documentation-accuracy defect: the ADR (docs/adr/0001-architecture.md:70) claims the CLI demo 'asserts' the same event sequence for both paths, but crates/voicekit-cli has zero tests. The property is empirically true (P2 vs P4 sequences matched), but nothing enforces it. Fix is a one-line ADR wording change or a small CLI parity test.

The scaffold invariants that must be preserved are intact across all four lenses: turn.rs/audio.rs/clock.rs/error.rs are unmodified vs HEAD, illegal TurnState transitions still surface as VoicekitError::Protocol (turn.rs:135-139, asserted at session.rs:630-638), Instant::now() appears only in clock.rs:67 with exactly one MonoClock per session, no base64/whole-turn JSON audio, provider traits remain streaming with a CancellationToken on every call, barge-in is token+generation-id with no sleep/race, process spawning is confined to voicekit-sidecar, and edit scope is clean apart from the explicitly mandated root Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock.
